images.title: Runs in each over
images.purpose: Show runs per over for two teams as a double bar graph with wickets marked, so the match story can be read.
images.composition: A double column graph: overs 1 to 20 along the bottom, runs up the side, a legend at the top.
exact_structure: A vertical axis from 0 to 20 with numbered gridlines at 0, 5, 10, 15 and 20 (scale 1 unit = 5 runs), captioned Runs.
Overs 1 to 20 along the horizontal axis, captioned Overs.
Teal (#0072B2) Blue team columns for overs 1 to 20 with heights 2, 11, 8, 7, 9, 6, 3, 4, 9, 8, 6, 15, 6, 9, 4, 10, 9, 13, 17, 7.
Vermilion (#D55E00) Red team columns for overs 1 to 18 with heights 10, 8, 4, 2, 11, 8, 3, 6, 10, 9, 9, 5, 16, 11, 9, 7, 7, 17; overs 19 and 20 have no red column.
Small hollow circles sit on top of the Blue team columns for overs 1, 3, 6, 13, 18, 19 and 20, one circle each, marking wickets. No circles on Red team columns.
A legend: a teal square labelled Blue team, a vermilion square labelled Red team, a hollow circle labelled Wicket.
images.takeaway: The team whose bars stop early reached its target, so it batted second and won.
images.description: A double bar graph of runs per over for two cricket teams with wicket circles on the blue team's bars.
images.context: Shown beside the concept text and video for this concept.
images.teaching_notes: Ask why the red bars stop after over 18 before reading any value.

image_decisions.why: The match story is read from the bars and wicket circles.
